layout_dets.text: The Effect of Nitrogen Additions Upon the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pitting Resistance of 18 Pct Cr, 18 Pct Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stainless Steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. G. HARTLINE, III

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of nitrogen additions upon the pitting resistance of 18 pct Cr, 18 pct Mn stain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less steel has been investigated by potentiokinetic techniques in a 1000 ppm NaCl solution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nitrogen additions increased the pitting resistance of the steel irrespective of structure,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: however, the ferritic steel was less pit resistant than the (duplex) steels containing both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite and ferrite which, in turn, were less pit resistant than the totally austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels. For steels having a duplex structure, the effect of nitrogen on the pitting resis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance was observed to follow a linear function of the relative amount of austenite in these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels due to the area effects of the austenite and ferrite which are galvanically coupled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in these steels. The addition of nitrogen was found to increase the amount of austenite at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a rate of approximately 200 times the percent nitrogen addition from 36 pct austenite for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 0.02 pct N steel to 100 pct for the 0.40 pct nitrogen steel. The addition of nitrogen to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the totally austenitic steels increased the pitting resistance at the rate of approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.31 volts per pct nitrogen added, but no mechanism was found for the increased resis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recent interest because of the increasing cost of nickel,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the expanded interest in CrMn steels, and the demands

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for higher strength austenitic stainless steels. Nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen additions were made in the Cr(Ni)Mn stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels to augment the austenitizing power of Mn. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the primary interest in the development of Cr(Ni)Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel was for cost reduction, sufficient nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen solubility existed in these steels to take advantage

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the strengthening effect of the nitrogen addition. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development of the Cr(Ni)Mn stainless steel culminated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a series of steels possessing similar corrosion re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance and equal or greater strength than the AISI 300

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: series stainless steels. While the general austenitizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and strengthening effects of N additions have been stud-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ied, the effects of N upon the degree of austenite stabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ization and the pitting resistance of the Cr(Ni)Mn steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have not been extensively studied.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NITROGEN bearing stainless steels have attracted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Early investigations¹-ª indicated that nitrogen addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions had little or no effect upon the pitting resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of stable austenitic stainless steels; however, these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results were obtained from alloys having such low ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen solubilities that the effect of nitrogen additions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: might not have been discernible. However, studies⁴-⁸

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of less stable alloys showed improvement in pitting re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sistance as the result of nitrogen additions. This in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased pitting resistance was attributed to the elimi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nation of ferrite (which is normally detrimental to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance of austenitic stainless steels).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: H. H. Uhlig⁴ examined the effect of crystal structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and nitrogen additions to the 18 Cr, 8 Ni (Type 304)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel. While this grade is usually considered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic, Uhlig transformed the alloy to ferrite by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowering the carbon and nitrogen contents and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quenching from elevated temperatures where the fer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ritic phase was stable. Uhlig found that the change in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crystal structure did not appreciably change the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance and, in fact, the ferritic structure displayed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minimally better pitting resistance than the commercia.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic grade. Uhlig also added 0.24 pct nitrogen to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Type 304. Tests in ferric chloride indicated that this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition increased the pitting resistance of Type 304

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from 2 to 10 times when compared with the commercial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic grade or the ferritic samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: M. A. Streicher® also investigated the effect of nitro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen and other alloy additions to Type 304 and found that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing the molybdenum, nitrogen and/or silicon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contents and reducing the carbon content increased

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pitting resistance of this steel. This investigation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concluded that the benefit of nitrogen additions to Type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 304 was through the elimination of the ferrite produced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the addition of molybdenum or silicon from the mi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crostructure. This conclusion follows from the work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Odar and Smith¹º where 18 Cr, 8 Ni alloys containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite and ferrite displayed inferior pitting resis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance to the totally austenitic steel. Streicher found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that increased pitting resistance resulted from the ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dition of nitrogen to the totally austenitic steels, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the benefit was relatively small unless accompanied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the addition of molybdenum and/or silicon.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While recent studies-1² have further indicated the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benefit of nitrogen additions to the Cr(Ni)Mn family of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels, the exact effect of nitrogen has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: partially masked because of changes in alloy content,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly additions of chromium and molybdenum.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The conclusions are also clouded because these stud-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ies like those above appear partially contradictory.

layout_dets.text: DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is clear from the results described above that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition of nitrogen increases the pitting resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18 Cr, 18 Mn steel. The addition of nitrogen to duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels eliminated ferrite (which decreased the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance) and was in agreement with the results ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained by Streicher° and by Odar and Smith.1º This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study also has shown that the addition of nitrogen in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creases the pitting resistance of totally austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels. While this was in agreement with the studies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of both Uhlig⁴ and Streicher,º the effect of nitrogen ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served in this work was more pronounced than that ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served by Streicher® in that no molybdenum or silicon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition was required in addition to the nitrogen for in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased pitting resistance. Finally, the totally ferritic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel was found to be inferior to the nitrogen austeni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tized steel. While this effect of structure is not in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agreement with that observed by Uhlig for the 18 Cr,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8 Ni steel, the addition of 0.40 pct nitrogen in the au-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stenitic 18 Cr. 18 Mn steel imparts additional corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to this steel such that comparison with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferritic 18 Cr, 18 Mn steel without nitrogen cannot be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made directly.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The relation between the pitting potential and amount

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of austenite in steels bears further explanation. Since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the austenite and ferrite are galvanically coupled, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential of the couple lies between the potential of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite and the ferrite as described by Fontana and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Greene²¹ for galvanic couples of dissimilar metals.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fontana and Greene describe the effect of altering the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas of the metals galvanically coupled and conclude

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that as the area of the more noble metal is increased

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the corrosion potential increases. The addition of ni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trogen to the duplex steels increases the amount and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the area of the austenite, the more noble phase in these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys. Therefore, the pitting potential of duplex alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has increased by the mechanism described above and
